title: Rollout-controller: consume SLO monitors (latency + error) w/ caching + guardrails
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
Auto-rollback requires the rollout-controller to evaluate latency + error SLOs for the specific rollout target (route/model/version/region/tier) using standardized monitor identities. This ticket implements the monitor consumption client and caching layer used by the policy evaluator.

Goal
- Provide a resilient, rate-limited client in rollout-controller to resolve + query SLO monitors (latency + error) using the canonical identity contract (ADR-0147).
- Add caching to avoid hammering monitoring backends and reduce evaluator lag.
- Define failure behavior so that monitoring outages/staleness do not cause unsafe rollbacks.

Non-goals
- Defining policy semantics (handled in ENG-2314 / ADR-0148)
- Building/owning monitor creation (handled via monitor migration ENG-2322 + observability work)

Implementation details
1) Monitor identity -> monitor lookup
- Input: canonical identity labels (route_id, model_id, model_version, region, customer_tier, slo_type=[latency|error], metric_scope=[serving|gateway], plus environment)
- Provide a single resolver API: ResolveMonitor(identity) -> monitor_handle (opaque ID + query template pointer)
- Enforce label normalization (case, unknown values) and explicit validation errors for missing required labels.

2) Query execution
- Provide QuerySLO(monitor_handle, window, now) -> SLO datapoint(s) needed by evaluator (p95 latency, error rate, total requests, timestamp)
- Use standardized query templates (observability pack) so rollout-controller isn’t hardcoding metric names.
- Timeout defaults: 2s per request with hedged retry (1 retry) only for idempotent reads.

3) Caching
- Two-level cache:
  - L1: in-process cache (per rollout-controller instance)
  - L2: shared cache (Redis) to reduce thundering herd across instances
- Cache keys:
  - monitor resolution cache: identity -> monitor_handle (TTL 10m)
  - query result cache: monitor_handle+window -> latest datapoint (TTL 15s)
- Negative caching:
  - monitor not found: cache 60s (so we don’t repeatedly spam for monitors that aren’t migrated yet)
  - permission/4xx (except 429): cache 5m and surface as config/identity error
- Stale data handling:
  - If cached datapoint is older than max_staleness (default 2m), return UNKNOWN verdict upstream (do not treat as breach).

4) Rate limiting + backoff
- Add per-instance concurrency cap for monitoring queries (default 20 inflight)
- Add token-bucket global limiter per tenant to avoid “cascade rollback” scenario when monitor backend is degraded.
- Respect 429 responses: exponential backoff with jitter, do not retry immediately.

5) Observability
- Emit internal metrics:
  - rollout.slo_monitor_client.resolve_latency_ms
  - rollout.slo_monitor_client.query_latency_ms
  - rollout.slo_monitor_client.cache_hit_ratio (L1/L2)
  - rollout.slo_monitor_client.errors_total (by class: timeout, 429, 5xx, not_found, invalid_identity)
  - rollout.slo_monitor_client.stale_datapoint_total
- Add structured logs with request_id, rollout_id, identity hash (not raw tenant identifiers), backend status.

Error handling contract (what evaluator receives)
- SUCCESS: datapoint + timestamp
- CONFIG_ERROR: invalid identity labels / authz / persistent 4xx -> should surface in Console as misconfiguration
- TRANSIENT_ERROR: timeouts/5xx/429 -> evaluator treats as UNKNOWN (no rollback) unless policy explicitly fail-closed (policy work elsewhere)
- NOT_FOUND: monitor missing -> UNKNOWN + emits event for migration gap

Acceptance criteria
- Can resolve and query both latency and error SLO monitors for a rollout target using ADR-0147 identity labels.
- Cache prevents repeated queries for the same monitor/window across repeated evaluation ticks (visible via cache_hit_ratio).
- Under monitoring outage (timeouts/5xx), evaluator receives UNKNOWN (no rollback triggered) and alertable metrics/logs are emitted.
- Under monitor staleness (no new data beyond max_staleness), returns UNKNOWN and increments stale counter.
- Rate limiting prevents >20 concurrent monitoring requests per instance and backs off on 429.
- Unit tests cover: identity validation, cache TTLs/negative caching, retry/backoff logic, staleness handling.
- Integration test stub wired so ENG-2320 can simulate breach by swapping monitor backend responses.

Links
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/auto-rollback-slo-integration-prd
- ADR-0147: confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0147-monitor-identity-contract
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/auto-rollback-slo-integration-design-spec
- Related: ENG-2314 (evaluator semantics), ENG-2322 (monitor labeling migration), INT-3310 (missing labels)

Rollout plan (for this component)
- Behind feature flag: rollout.slo_monitor_client.enabled
- Enable for internal canaries first; verify cache hit ratio + query volume; then expand to low-risk tenants.
comments: 2025-02-12 (Benji Okafor): Drafted client interface. Proposal: keep resolver + query in single package so evaluator can mock a single dependency. Need confirmation from Observability on whether monitor lookup is by labels->monitor_id or by templated query only.

2025-02-14 (Nadia Rahman): Monitoring API can support label-based lookup but needs strict label normalization. Please don’t send raw route names; use route_id. Also note data freshness can lag 30-60s depending on region—make staleness threshold configurable.

2025-02-18 (Jordan Lee): For policy engine we need explicit error classes (CONFIG vs TRANSIENT vs NOT_FOUND) so we can render meaningful Console verdicts. Please ensure the error includes a stable code and human-readable message.
2025-02-20 (Sean Gallagher): Please avoid rollback on UNKNOWN by default. Also add a counter for stale datapoints—this bit us in the Feb regression (we were looking at old data).

2025-02-24 (Benji Okafor): Implemented L1 cache + Redis L2, TTLs as described. Added 429 backoff and a hard cap of 20 inflight. Next: finalize negative cache behavior for 404 monitor not found (suggest 60s).
2025-02-27 (Ethan Park): LGTM on approach. Make sure the identity validation rejects missing region/tier, otherwise we’ll query global monitors and silently mask per-tenant issues.

2025-03-03 (Benji Okafor): Open question: should resolve cache TTL be 10m or 60m? I’m leaning 10m because monitor migration is active and we want missing monitors to show up relatively quickly without restart.
2025-03-05 (Benji Okafor): Merged. Added metrics + structured logs. Wired mock backend for ENG-2320 harness. Marking Done.
